newsitem.title: USA: Motorola automotive group gets sector status.
newsitem.headline: Motorola automotive group gets sector status.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Wednesday that its Automotive, Energy and Controls Group has achieved sector status, a designation that usually means a business has annual revenues of more than $2 billion.
A spokeswoman later said the business group, which is being renamed the Automotive, Energy and Components Sector, has achieved at least $2.0 billion in annual sales.

No prior sales comparisons were given. Previously, Automotive, Energy and Controls sales were reported in a miscellaneous business category, which in 1995 had sales of $3.35 billion, the spokeswoman said. That category also included satellite and space technology and new ventures.
The business name change reflects the growth of the Components Group within the sector, Motorola said.

The company said Frederick Tucker, 56, executive vice president and general manager, was named president and general manager of the new sector. The Ceramic Products Division plant in Albuquerque, N.M., is part of the new sector.
Motorola, which makes wireless communications and electronic systems and semiconductors, had 1995 sales of $27.0 billion.
